bibliographic.title: Balancing risks and benefits: clinicians' perspectives on the use of generative AI chatbots in mental healthcare
bibliographic.authors: Lyndsey Hipgrave, Jessie Goldie, Simon Dennis, Amanda Coleman
bibliographic.citation_apa: Hipgrave, L., Goldie, J., Dennis, S., & Coleman, A. (2025). Balancing risks and benefits: clinicians' perspectives on the use of generative AI chatbots in mental healthcare. Frontiers in Digital Health, 7, 1606291. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2025.1606291

methodology.method_family: qualitative interviews with scale-based questions and chatbot demonstration
methodology.study_design: 45-minute virtual semi-structured interviews with open-ended and scale-based questions plus screen-recorded ChatGPT 4o chatbot demonstration
methodology.technology_context: generative-AI chatbots in mental healthcare; demonstration used GPTs created using ChatGPT 4o

eligibility.decision_rationale: Primary empirical study directly examining mental health clinicians' perspectives on integrating generative-AI chatbots, reporting benefits, risks, and contextual governance concerns including privacy, regulation, bias, and inappropriate recommendations in a regulated healthcare setting.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methods/results pages were provided; full analysis, ethics, and limitations sections were not available for complete appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Clear objective and interview protocol described; sample size stated. Qualitative analysis procedures, ethics approval, and study limitations are not present in the supplied text, limiting rigor and reflexivity assessment.

cerqual.explanation: Findings coherently report clinician-identified benefits and risks of generative AI chatbots in mental healthcare with direct relevance to conversational AI governance in a regulated domain, but appraisal is constrained because analysis methods and limitations are absent from the provided excerpt.

coding.theme: Contextual balancing of risks and benefits in generative AI chatbot adoption in mental healthcare
coding.subtheme: Clinician-identified governance and safety concerns for conversational AI tools

synthesis.main_claim: Mental health clinicians identify both benefits and risks of generative-AI chatbots without a significant overall preference for either, and the balance is highly contextual depending on use case and population served.
synthesis.contribution: Provides stakeholder insights from mental health clinicians on benefits, risks, and governance-related concerns to inform future development of AI chatbot tools in mental healthcare.
synthesis.use_in_review: Central evidence on clinician governance perspectives for generative AI chatbots in regulated mental healthcare, especially regarding privacy, lack of regulation, bias, hallucinations, inappropriate recommendations, and contextual risk-benefit trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Study aims to explore clinicians' perspectives on risks and benefits of generative-AI chatbots in mental health
evidence.excerpt: This paper aimed to explore the perspectives of mental health clinicians regarding the risks and benefits of integrating generative-AI chatbots into the mental health landscape.

evidence.claim: Empirical design with 23 clinician virtual interviews and chatbot demonstration
evidence.excerpt: Twenty-three clinicians participated in a 45-minute virtual interview, in which a series of open-ended and scale-based questions were asked, and a demonstration of a mental health chatbot's potential capabilities was presented.

evidence.claim: Clinicians identified governance-related risks including lack of regulation and privacy concerns
evidence.excerpt: they also identified risks, including the lack of regulation, data and privacy concerns, chatbots' limited understanding of client backgrounds

evidence.claim: Risk-benefit balance is contextual and not dominated by either side
evidence.excerpt: Qualitative responses revealed that the balance of risks and benefits is highly contextual, varying based on the use case and the population group being served.

evidence.claim: Generative AI chatbots pose unpredictability, hallucination, and bias risks
evidence.excerpt: It also risks generating "hallucinations," where the AI generates information that is incorrect, misleading, or entirely fabricated

evidence.claim: Lack of comprehensive regulatory frameworks is a documented concern
evidence.excerpt: Other concerns include AI's handling of disclosures of criminal activity (29), the lack of comprehensive regulatory frameworks (30, 31)

evidence.claim: Safe integration requires robust regulatory frameworks
evidence.excerpt: Mitigating risks and ensuring safe, effective integration into mental healthcare requires careful consideration, collaboration, and robust regulatory frameworks.

evidence.claim: Demonstration used ChatGPT 4o GPTs in a mental health triage scenario
evidence.excerpt: The demonstration featured a screen-recorded video of a series of GPTs created using ChatGPT 4o.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed journal article in Frontiers in Digital Health
evidence.excerpt: CITATION Hipgrave L, Goldie J, Dennis S and Coleman A (2025) Balancing risks and benefits: clinicians' perspectives on the use of generative AI chatbots in mental healthcare. Front. Digit. Health 7:1606291.

evidence.claim: Chatbot demonstration did not significantly shift risk-benefit preference
evidence.excerpt: a demonstration of potential chatbot capabilities was not found to influence whether participants favoured the risks or benefits of chatbots.
